steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the 600g chicken breast into strips and season with salt and pepper. Even strips cook quickly and evenly.

Browning the chicken: Brown the chicken in part of the 30g butter for 4-5 minutes per side, then remove. Important: don't overcrowd the pan, or the chicken will steam instead of browning — cook in batches if needed.
Sautéing the mushrooms: In the same pan, sauté the 400g mushrooms over high heat until browned and their moisture has evaporated. This develops flavor and keeps the sauce from becoming watery.
Aromatics: Add 1 finely chopped onion, 2 garlic cloves and thyme, and sauté until softened.
Deglazing with wine: Deglaze with the 100ml white wine and let the alcohol evaporate, scraping up the bottom of the pan. The caramelized bits left behind add depth to the sauce.

Finishing the sauce: Pour in the 200ml cream, return the chicken to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Important: keep the heat low after adding the cream, as a hard boil can cause it to split.
Serving: Taste, adjust salt and pepper, and serve hot.
kotopoulo_manitaria.plate: With rice or mashed potatoes, mushrooms on top.

steps: Preparing the meat: Slice each chicken fillet horizontally through the middle to make it thinner. Place the pieces between two sheets of parchment paper and pound them with a meat mallet until about 1 cm thick. Important: an even, thin thickness is the secret to a schnitzel that cooks quickly and stays juicy without the coating burning.
Seasoning: Season the cutlets well with salt and pepper on both sides. Let them come to room temperature for 10 minutes.

Setting up the breading station: Prepare three plates. Put the flour in the first, the beaten eggs with a little salt in the second, and the breadcrumbs mixed with the parmesan and garlic powder in the third.

Breading: Coat each fillet first in flour (shaking off the excess), then in egg, and finally in breadcrumbs, pressing well so the coating sticks all over. Important: press the breadcrumbs on firmly by hand for an even, crisp crust.
Heating the oil: Heat the sunflower oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. It's ready when a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles immediately on contact (about 170-180°C).
Frying: Fry the cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Don't overcrowd the pan, or the temperature will drop.
Draining: Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to drain off excess oil.
Serving: Serve hot with lemon wedges for squeezing over.
kotopoulo_pane.wine: A crisp dry white or ice-cold beer.
kotopoulo_pane.plate: Serve with french fries and a refreshing green salad.

steps: Browning the chicken: Season the thighs with salt and pepper and brown them in olive oil on all sides for 4-5 minutes. Remove and set aside. This locks in the juices.
Base: In the same pan, sauté the onion for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and both paprikas. Stir for 1 minute over low heat. Important: paprika burns easily over high heat and turns bitter.
Simmering: Add the tomato, thyme and ½ cup water. Return the chicken to the pan. Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Finishing: Remove the chicken. Stir the cream into the sauce and let it thicken for 2 minutes. Serve the chicken topped with the sauce, with rice or mashed potatoes.
kotopoulo_paprika.plate: With a rich paprika sauce and rice.

steps: Browning the chicken: Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper and brown them on all sides in hot oil, 3-4 minutes per side. Browning seals in the juices and adds depth of flavor.
Sautéing: Remove the chicken, sauté the onion and garlic in the same oil for 5 minutes.
Sauce: Add the tomato, cinnamon, allspice and salt. Return the chicken to the pot. Simmer covered for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Adding the rice: Remove the chicken, measure the liquid in the pot and add stock so you have 3 cups total. Add the rice and stir.
Cooking the rice: Simmer covered for 18 minutes over low heat. IMPORTANT: do not stir while it cooks.
Serving: Place the chicken on top of the rice, cover and let stand for 5 minutes.
kotopoulo_rizi.plate: Rice as the base with chicken on top.

steps: Cutting: Cut the breast into 2.5cm cubes. Even size means even cooking.
Marinade: Mix olive oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, paprika and yogurt. The yogurt tenderizes the meat and helps keep it juicy.
Marinating: Let the cubes sit in the marinade for at least 30 minutes (2-3 hours is better). IMPORTANT: salt only lightly, just before grilling.
Skewering: Thread 5-6 cubes onto each skewer without packing them too tightly.
Grilling: Grill over a very hot grill for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes for even browning. Chicken breast cooks fast — don't overcook it.
Serving: Serve in pita or on a plate with tzatziki, tomato and onion.
Marinade: Mix the olive oil, lemon, grated garlic, oregano, thyme and paprika. Score the thighs with a knife so the marinade penetrates deeply.
Marinating: Coat the thighs with the marinade and let them sit at least 1 hour in the refrigerator — ideally overnight. IMPORTANT: salt only 30 minutes before grilling so the meat doesn't dry out.
Preheating: Preheat the grill or griddle to a high temperature. Clean it and brush with oil so the chicken doesn't stick.
Grilling: Grill the thighs over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes per side. Start skin-side down ("butterflied") for crispy skin.
Checking doneness: Use a meat thermometer — 75°C internal, or the juices should run clear. IMPORTANT: don't cut into it to check, as you'll lose the juices.
Resting: Let it rest for 5 minutes covered with foil before serving so the juices redistribute.
kotopoulo_sxara.plate: With lemon, oregano and lemon potatoes.

ing: Chicken thigh fillet 700 g, cut into bite-sized pieces
Red and green peppers, 3, cut into strips
Grated tomato or tomato juice 3 tbsp
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
steps: Preparing the chicken: Cut the thigh fillet into 3-4 cm pieces and pat dry well with paper towels so it browns properly.

Frying the chicken: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan or wok over high heat and add the chicken pieces. Important: Don't overcrowd the pan - fry in batches if needed, so the meat sears and browns instead of stewing in its own juices.
Browning: Let the chicken brown well on all sides, about 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Adding the vegetables: Add the onion and peppers to the pan and sauté for 4-5 minutes until slightly softened while still keeping some crunch.
Garlic and deglazing with wine: Add the garlic, stir for 30 seconds and deglaze with the white wine, letting the alcohol evaporate.
Tomato and cooking: Add the grated tomato, oregano, salt and pepper. Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Final check: Taste and adjust the salt, making sure the chicken is cooked through without drying out.
Serving: Serve piping hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice on top, accompanied by fried potatoes or pilaf rice.
kotopoulo_tigania.wine: Dry white wine from Crete, such as Vidiano, cool and aromatic
kotopoulo_tigania.plate: Served on a plate with fried potatoes or pilaf rice, accompanied by a Greek village salad

ing: Gruyère or Emmental cheese, grated, 100 g
steps: Boiling the chicken: Boil the chicken fillets in lightly salted water for 15-18 minutes until softened, drain and let cool.
Making the béchamel: Melt the butter in a pot, add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes over low heat so the raw flour taste cooks off. Gradually pour in the hot milk, whisking.

Important: The béchamel must be very thick, almost paste-like, so it holds its shape when cold and doesn't melt during frying. Simmer over low heat, stirring constantly, until well thickened, about 10 minutes.
Enriching the sauce: Remove from the heat, add the grated cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper, stir to incorporate, and let the béchamel cool completely, preferably in the fridge for 1-2 hours.
Assembling: Slice the chicken, place a slice of ham between two chicken slices and spread the cold, thick béchamel generously over the whole surface as a coating.

Coating: Dip each piece first in the beaten egg and then in the breadcrumbs, pressing well so they stick all over. Repeat the egg-and-breadcrumb process for a double coating, so the crust doesn't break during frying.

Frying: Heat plenty of oil over medium-high heat and fry the pieces until evenly browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side, so the béchamel inside warms through without melting and leaking out.
Serving: Drain on paper towels and serve immediately, hot, while the crust is still crispy.
kotopoulo_vigeroua.wine: Dry white wine, Assyrtiko from Santorini or a light Roditis
kotopoulo_vigeroua.plate: Serve with mashed potatoes or cabbage-and-carrot salad and a little lemony mayonnaise on the side

steps: Making the broth: Place the whole chicken in a pot with cold water along with the 2 carrots and celery, and boil for 45 minutes. Important: skim off the foam that rises at the start with a slotted spoon, so the broth stays clear and clean-tasting.
Boning: Remove the chicken, let it cool slightly, and bone it into bite-sized pieces. Strain the broth to remove any small bones.
Cooking the rice: Bring the broth back to a boil and add the 100g rice. Boil for 15 minutes until tender. Taste and adjust the salt.
Whisking the avgolemono: Whisk the 2 eggs with the juice of 1 lemon until frothy. Whisking well makes the avgolemono light and prevents it from curdling.

Tempering: Gradually add ladlefuls of hot broth to the egg-lemon mixture, whisking constantly. Important: this step is crucial for gradually raising the temperature of the mixture, because if the eggs go straight into the hot broth they will curdle and form lumps.
Combining off the heat: Remove the pot from the heat and pour in the avgolemono, stirring. Do not return it to a strong boil, or it will curdle.
Serving: Add the boned chicken, sprinkle with fresh dill, and serve hot.
kotosopa.plate: In a deep bowl, with chicken and dill.

steps: Boiling: Place the chicken in cold water (2.5 liters) with carrots, celery, onion, and salt. Simmer over low heat for 45-50 minutes, skimming off the foam during the first few minutes.
Soup base: Remove the chicken and strain the stock. Cut the meat into pieces.
Rice: Return the stock to the pot, bring to a boil, and add the rice. Cook for 15-18 minutes.
Adding the meat: Return the chicken pieces to the pot. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Serving without avgolemono: Serve immediately in deep bowls.

Avgolemono (optional): If making avgolemono, whisk 2 eggs with the juice of 1 lemon until frothy. Gradually add 2-3 ladles of hot soup while whisking constantly (tempering). Pour back into the pot and stir in a circular motion. Important: DO NOT let it boil afterward, or the egg will curdle.
kotosoupa.plate: In a deep bowl, served hot.

steps: Toasting the almonds: Toast the ground almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they smell fragrant, then let them cool completely. Important: raw ground almond tastes flat, and toasting is what wakes the flavour.
Beating the butter: Beat the butter with the sugar for 5 minutes.
Adding the egg: Add the egg and the almond extract and beat until smooth.
Combining: Mix in the flour, the cooled ground almonds and the baking powder to a soft dough.
Important: Ground almond carries fat but no gluten, so this dough is more fragile than usual. Handle it gently and do not knead it.
Chilling: Chill the dough for 30 minutes so the butter firms up and it holds its shape.
Shaping: Roll into balls and flatten them slightly, or form the traditional crescent shape.
Decorating: Press a whole almond into the centre of each and brush with lightly beaten egg white.
Baking: Bake at 170°C for 20-22 minutes. Important: keep the temperature low — ground almond burns far faster than flour and turns bitter.
Cooling: Leave them on the tray for 5 minutes before moving them, because they are very fragile while hot.
koulourakia_amygdalou.wine: Amaretto or a sweet white wine.
koulourakia_amygdalou.plate: Serve on a platter with whole almonds scattered between them.

steps: Sifting the cocoa: Sift the cocoa together with the flour twice. Important: cocoa clumps stubbornly and unsifted lumps leave dry bitter pockets in the dough.
Beating the butter: Beat the butter with the sugar for 5 minutes until light.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Making the dough: Add the sifted dry ingredients gradually with the milk, mixing to a soft dough.
Important: Cocoa absorbs more liquid than flour. If the dough feels dry and cracks, add milk a spoonful at a time — never all at once.
Resting: Rest the dough for 30 minutes so it hydrates fully.
Shaping: Roll into ropes and form twists or rings, all the same size.
Important: Do not brush these with egg. On a dark dough the glaze is invisible, and the sugar in the yolk burns before the biscuit is done.
Baking: Bake at 175°C for 18-20 minutes — slightly lower than usual, because the dark colour hides burning until it is too late.
Testing: They are ready when the base is firm and they lift cleanly off the tray. Dust with icing sugar once cold.
koulourakia_kakao.plate: Serve on a platter dusted with icing sugar for contrast with the dark colour.

steps: Warming the honey: Warm the honey gently until it flows freely. Important: never let it boil — high heat destroys its aroma and leaves only sweetness behind.
Mixing the liquids: Whisk the warm honey with the olive oil, the orange juice and the sugar until combined.
Adding the spices: Stir in the cinnamon and cloves, which need the liquid to distribute evenly.
Making the dough: Add the sifted flour with the baking powder gradually, mixing to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Important: Honey dough is always stickier than butter dough. Do not add extra flour to fix it — oil your hands instead.
Resting: Rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Shaping: Shape into small ropes or ovals with oiled hands and press sesame seeds onto the surface.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Important: Watch them closely from minute 15. Honey caramelises and burns much faster than sugar, and they go from golden to black quickly.
Finishing: Drizzle with a little extra warm honey while still hot, so it soaks in rather than sitting on the surface.
koulourakia_meliou.plate: Serve drizzled with a little honey and sprinkled with sesame seeds.

steps: Preparing the oranges: Zest the oranges before juicing them, taking only the coloured layer.
Beating the butter: Beat the soft butter with the sugar for 5 minutes, until pale and creamy.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, then the orange juice, zest and vanilla.
Important: The mixture will look split at this point. This is normal — the flour brings it back together.
Adding the flour: Sift the flour with the baking powder and add it gradually, mixing until a soft dough forms.
Important: Stop kneading the moment the dough comes together. Over-kneaded dough makes hard koulourakia instead of crumbly ones.
Resting: Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes at room temperature — not in the fridge, or it becomes too stiff to shape.
Shaping: Roll pieces into ropes and form twists, plaits or rings, keeping them all the same thickness so they bake evenly.
Brushing: Brush with beaten egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden. Important: they firm up as they cool, so take them out while still slightly soft or they turn rock hard.
koulourakia_portokaliou.plate: Serve on a platter or in a glass jar, with coffee alongside.

steps: Preparing the vanilla: Split the pods lengthwise and scrape out the seeds with a knife tip. Important: real pods give a depth and speckled look that no extract can match.
Infusing the sugar: Rub the vanilla seeds into the sugar with your fingertips, so the aroma spreads through every grain.
Beating: Beat the butter with the vanilla sugar for 6 minutes until white and airy.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, then the milk.
Making the dough: Sift in the flour with the baking powder and salt and mix to a soft dough.
Resting: Rest for 30 minutes.
Shaping: Roll into ropes and form small rings or S-shapes, keeping them small — these are meant to be delicate.
Baking: Bake at 175°C for 18 minutes. Important: they must stay pale. Browning masks the vanilla, which is the whole point of the biscuit.
Dusting while warm: Roll them in icing sugar while still warm, so the first coat sticks and melts into the surface.
Second coat: Once cold, roll them a second time so they end up properly white.
koulourakia_vanilias.plate: Serve on a platter with plenty of icing sugar on top.

steps: Choosing the butter: Use real butter, not margarine. Important: in a recipe this plain, the butter is the entire flavour — there is nothing to hide behind.
Softening: Leave the butter out until it yields to finger pressure but is not melted or oily.
Beating: Beat it with the sugar for 6 minutes, until genuinely white and doubled in volume.
Adding the eggs: Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, milk and salt.
Adding the flour: Sift in the flour with the baking powder and mix until a soft, non-sticky dough forms.
Resting: Rest the dough for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates and it becomes easier to shape.
Shaping: Roll into ropes about 1.5 cm thick and shape into S-forms, rings or twists.
Important: Do not make them too thick. Butter koulourakia spread as they bake, and thick ones stay raw in the middle.
Brushing: Brush with egg yolk thinned with a little milk, for an even golden shine.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes, and cool them on a rack so the bottoms do not soften from trapped steam.
koulourakia_voutyrou.plate: Arrange fanned out on a platter, dusted with icing sugar.

steps: Cut the cauliflower into florets and boil for 8 minutes. Drain.
Spread in a baking pan, drizzle with oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, until lightly golden.
Pour the béchamel over the top and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for another 15 minutes until golden and gratinéed.

Beating the butter: With the 250g clarified butter at room temperature, beat in the mixer for about 15 minutes until it turns pale and fluffy like a cream. The long beating incorporates air and gives the kourabiedes their light texture.
Adding the liquids: Add the 1 egg yolk, the vanilla and the 100g powdered sugar and keep beating until combined.
Toasting the almonds: If not already toasted, lightly toast the 100g almonds and chop them into small pieces. Toasting makes them crunchy and aromatic.

Kneading: Sift the 500g flour and fold it in gradually together with the almonds, kneading lightly. IMPORTANT: don't overknead and don't let the dough warm from your hands, as this melts the butter and toughens the kourabiedes.
Shaping: Shape into half-moons or stars and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving gaps between them as they puff up slightly.
Baking: Bake at 170°C for 18-22 minutes, until set without taking on much color — kourabiedes should stay pale.
Finishing: While still warm, generously dust them with the 200g powdered sugar. The warm surface makes the sugar stick and form the characteristic white coating.
kourabiedes.plate: On a platter, dusted all over like snow with powdered sugar.

steps: Sautéing: In a pot, sauté 2 chopped onions until softened, then add the 600g ground beef and brown it well, breaking it up, so it caramelizes rather than stewing in its own liquid.
Meat sauce: Add the 200g grated tomato, cinnamon, allspice and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until almost dry. Important: the filling must be dry, otherwise it will make the phyllo soggy.
Cooling: Let the meat cool slightly, so the eggs don't cook as soon as you add them.
Finishing the filling: Mix the meat with 150g grated kefalotyri and 2 eggs. The eggs bind the filling so it doesn't fall apart when sliced.
Layering the sheets: Butter the baking pan and layer half the phyllo sheets, brushing each one with melted butter (from the 80g) to make them crisp and puffed.
Filling and sealing: Spread the filling, cover with the remaining buttered sheets and seal by folding the edges inward. Score the surface into pieces, so it can be cut easily after baking.
Baking: Bake at 180°C for 55-60 minutes until golden and crispy. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
Boiling the meat: Place the meat in cold water (3 liters). Boil, skimming off the foam for the first 10 minutes — the foam contains impurities and clouds the stock.
Vegetables: Add carrots, celery, onion, tomato, and salt. Simmer covered for 60-70 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Potatoes: Add the potatoes and cook for another 20 minutes.
Rice: Add the rice and cook for 15-18 minutes.
Finishing: Add lemon juice for freshness. Taste and adjust salt. Important: this soup tastes even better the next day.
kreatosopa.plate: In a deep bowl with a squeeze of lemon juice.

steps: Preparation: Cut the broccoli into florets and the potato into small cubes, and finely chop the onion and garlic.
Sautéing the base: In a pot, melt the butter with the olive oil and sauté the onion and garlic until glossy, without browning.
Adding the vegetables: Add the potato and broccoli and stir for 2-3 minutes so they absorb the aromas.
Boiling: Add the vegetable stock, salt, and pepper, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender.
Important: Do not cook longer than necessary, as prolonged boiling darkens the broccoli and it loses its bright green color.
Blending: Remove from the heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth and velvety, with no lumps.
Heavy cream: Return to low heat, add the heavy cream, and stir for 2 minutes until incorporated, without letting it boil.
Tasting and adjusting: Taste and adjust the salt and pepper; if too thick, add a little hot stock.
Serving: Serve hot in bowls with a swirl of cream on top and a few croutons.
krema_brokolou.wine: Dry white Assyrtiko wine or tsipouro
krema_brokolou.plate: Serve in a deep bowl with a spiral of cream and croutons in the center.

steps: Caramel: Put the 150g sugar with the 2 tbsp water in a pot and heat without stirring until it turns a red-brown color. IMPORTANT: don't stir the caramel with a spoon, as it will crystallize — just swirl the pot gently.
Lining the molds: As soon as the caramel is ready, quickly divide it among the molds before it sets, coating the bottom of each.
Custard mixture: Beat the 4 eggs with the 120g sugar and slowly pour in the warm milk (600ml) while stirring, so the eggs don't cook. Add vanilla.
Straining: Strain the mixture and divide it among the caramel-lined molds, so the custard comes out perfectly smooth without any egg clumps.
Baking in a bain-marie: Place the molds in a pan with hot water (bain-marie) and bake at 160°C for 45-50 minutes. The bain-marie ensures gentle, even baking without curdling the custard.
Chilling and unmolding: Refrigerate for 4 hours or more to set, then invert the mold onto a plate so the caramel runs over the top.

ing: Heavy cream 100 ml (or almond milk for a fasting/vegan version)
Breadcrumbs or dried dill, for garnish
steps: Preparing the vegetables: Peel and slice the carrots into rounds, finely chop the onion and leek, and cut the potato into cubes.
Sautéing: In a pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the onion and leek for 4-5 minutes until softened, without coloring.
Adding the carrots: Add the carrots and potato to the pot and stir for 2-3 minutes so they pick up flavor from the oil.
Boiling: Pour in the broth until the vegetables are covered, add salt and pepper, and simmer over low heat for 25-30 minutes until the carrots are very soft.
Important: The long, slow simmering is essential so the carrots break down easily when puréed and the soup comes out velvety with no lumps; check with a fork before proceeding.
Puréeing: Remove from the heat and purée with an immersion blender until smooth and creamy, adding a little broth if it's too thick.
Enriching with cream: Return the pot to low heat, add the cream and ginger, stir well and simmer for 5 minutes without letting it boil.
Serving: Serve hot in deep plates, garnishing with a drizzle of olive oil and toasted breadcrumbs or dill.
krema_karotou.wine: A fresh white Assyrtiko or a light Moschofilero pairs ideally with the sweetness of the carrot.
krema_karotou.plate: Serve in deep plates with a swirl of olive oil and a little fresh village bread on the side.

steps: Heat the milk with the vanilla until just below boiling, then take it off the heat and let it infuse for 10 minutes.
Beat the yolks with the sugar and the cornflour until pale and completely smooth.
Important: Pour the hot milk over the yolks slowly, in a thin stream, whisking without stopping. This tempering is the only thing standing between you and scrambled eggs.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook over medium heat, whisking constantly and reaching into the corners of the pan.
Important: Keep whisking especially where the base meets the sides — this is where cream always catches and burns first.
When it thickens, let it bubble for exactly 1 minute more. This cooks out the raw starch taste, which otherwise stays.
Take it off the heat and beat in the butter, which gives it shine and a silkier texture.
Pass it through a sieve if any lumps have formed — this rescues almost any cream.
Cover the surface directly with cling film so no skin forms, and refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Before using, beat it briefly with a whisk to loosen it back to a smooth cream.
krema_zaxaroplastikis.wine: Not applicable — a base for other desserts.
krema_zaxaroplastikis.plate: Use as a filling, or serve in small glasses with fruit and a biscuit.
